newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: GOVERNMENT GOES AFTER TAX EVADERS, BOOTLEGGERS.
newsitem.headline: GOVERNMENT GOES AFTER TAX EVADERS, BOOTLEGGERS.

text.p: The Lithuanian government said on Tuesday that the tax inspection had slapped a 774,000 litas fine on Lithuanian-German joint venture Max Entertainment as part of its crack-down on tax evasion and smuggling.
The government's press office said in a statement that the fine was imposed because the company was caught with illicit booze in stock.
"The fine of 774,000 litas makes 25 percent of the company's turnover over the last 12 months," the statement said.
The government also said that six thousand companies have been checked during the last few months and the total sum in fines was estimated at 6.5 million litas by May 15.
The statement said that the most frequent violations detected were trade in goods without necessary documents and the falsification of company books.
The government said earlier that its budget revenues for the first four months of the year were in surplus for the first time since 1992.
The government has declared war on tax evasion and vowed to stamp the practice out.
